# `silk/msgpack/scanner`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read MessagePack data as a sequence of tokens, without building a tree and without allocating.

## When to use
Use [`MsgpackScanner`](#MsgpackScanner) to read MessagePack bytes that are in one slice, token by token, when you
do not need a tree. To get a tree, use `silk.msgpack.value.Msgpack.parse`. To read your own
types, use `silk.schema.msgpack.SchemaMsgpack.decode`.

## Details
Each call of [`MsgpackScanner.next`](#MsgpackScanner.impl.next) reads one value header. A scalar is complete in its token.
An [`MsgpackToken.Array`](#MsgpackToken.Array) token is followed by the tokens of `count` values, and an
[`MsgpackToken.Map`](#MsgpackToken.Map) token by the tokens of `count` keys, each followed by its value. The scanner
does not track that nesting; the caller counts.

Integers of every width become [`MsgpackToken.Integer`](#MsgpackToken.Integer), or [`MsgpackToken.Unsigned`](#MsgpackToken.Unsigned) above the
largest `i64`. A 32-bit float is widened to `f64`. A string or binary token gives a
[`MsgpackSpan`](#MsgpackSpan) of its payload in the input; the UTF-8 of a string is checked. All offsets are
byte offsets from the start of the input.

## Errors
- [`MsgpackError`](#MsgpackError) with a [`MsgpackReason`](#MsgpackReason) and the offset of the problem. After an error, the
  scanner cannot continue. Make a new one.

## Gotchas
The scanner does not limit nesting and does not check for duplicate map keys. An extension
value, such as a timestamp (type -1), is returned as its type and payload, not interpreted.

## Examples
### Sum the integers of an array
```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.msgpack.scanner { MsgpackError, MsgpackScanner, MsgpackToken }

fn sum(input: &[u8]) -> i64 {
  let mut scanner = MsgpackScanner.make(input)
  let mut total: i64 = 0
  while true {
    match move MsgpackScanner.next(&mut scanner) {
      Result<MsgpackToken, MsgpackError>.Failure {..} => {
        return -1
      }
      Result<MsgpackToken, MsgpackError>.Success { value } => match move value {
        MsgpackToken.Integer { value: number } => {
          total = total + number
        }
        MsgpackToken.EndOfInput => {
          return total
        }
        _ => {}
      }
    }
  }
  return total
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // An array of 3 elements: 1, 200 (as a `uint 8`) and 5.
  if sum(b"\x93\x01\xcc\xc8\x05") != 206 {
    return 1
  }
  // The array says 3 elements but the input ends after one.
  if sum(b"\x93\x01") != -1 {
    return 2
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="MsgpackScanner"></a>

## `MsgpackScanner`

```silk
pub struct MsgpackScanner<'input>
```

A reader of the MessagePack tokens of one slice.

### When to use

Use it to read MessagePack without a tree: call [`MsgpackScanner.next`](#MsgpackScanner.impl.next) until it returns
`MsgpackToken.EndOfInput`.

### Details

The scanner borrows the input and holds only its position, so [`MsgpackScanner.fork`](#MsgpackScanner.impl.fork) is cheap.
It reads values one after another and does not require the input to be one value; the caller
decides what follows a complete value.

### Gotchas

After an error, the scanner cannot continue. Make a new one.

<a id="MsgpackScanner.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`


Returns a scanner at the start of `input`.

<a id="MsgpackScanner.impl.next"></a>

### Method `next`

```silk
pub fn next(self: &mut MsgpackScanner<'input>) -> Result<MsgpackToken, MsgpackError>
```

Returns the next token, or `EndOfInput` when no bytes are left.

#### Details

A string, binary or extension token is returned only when its whole payload is in the input.
An array or map token is returned only when the input has at least one byte left for each
element it counts, so `count` is never larger than the input.

#### Errors

- `MsgpackError` with `UnexpectedEnd` if the input ends inside the value, `ReservedByte` for
  the byte `0xc1`, or `InvalidUtf8` for a string that is not UTF-8. The scanner cannot
  continue.

<a id="MsgpackScanner.impl.peek"></a>

### Method `peek`

```silk
pub fn peek(self: &mut MsgpackScanner<'input>) -> Result<MsgpackToken, MsgpackError>
```

Returns the next token without consuming it. The next call of `next` returns the same token.

#### Errors

- `MsgpackError` with `UnexpectedEnd` if the input ends inside the value, `ReservedByte` for
  the byte `0xc1`, or `InvalidUtf8` for a string that is not UTF-8. The scanner cannot
  continue.

<a id="MsgpackScanner.impl.fork"></a>

### Method `fork`

```silk
pub fn fork(self: &MsgpackScanner<'input>) -> MsgpackScanner<'input>
```

Returns a scanner at the same position as `self`, which reads the same tokens next without
moving `self`.

#### When to use

Use it to look ahead more than one token, such as to find a key of a map before reading the
entries before it.

<a id="MsgpackScanner.impl.offset"></a>

### Method `offset`

```silk
pub fn offset(self: &MsgpackScanner<'input>) -> usize
```

Returns the byte offset of the last token that `next` or `peek` returned: the offset of its
first header byte. Use it for errors.

<a id="MsgpackScanner.impl.end"></a>

### Method `end`

```silk
pub fn end(self: &MsgpackScanner<'input>) -> usize
```

Returns the byte offset after the last token that `next` or `peek` returned: after the
payload of a scalar, or after the header of an array or a map.

<a id="MsgpackScanner.impl.length"></a>


<a id="MsgpackScanner.impl.slice"></a>

### Method `slice`

```silk
pub fn slice(self: &MsgpackScanner<'input>, span: MsgpackSpan) -> &'input [u8]
```

Returns the input bytes of `span`, such as the UTF-8 of a string token or the data of a
binary token.

#### Gotchas

Traps if `span` is not inside the input. A span from a token of this scanner always is.
